headline: Russia-linked spies target Ukraine war support; Harvard breach hits 851,000 accounts; Node-RED and Ivanti exploitation continues

bullets.text: New: The Record reports Russia-linked cyber spies targeting Ukraine's war crimes investigations and military aid routes. Help Net Security separately reports the Gorbag APT group hitting Ukrainian courts and city councils with self-deleting malware.
New: BleepingComputer reports a Harvard University data breach exposed information from 851,000 accounts. Have I Been Pwned has added 850,537 of them.
New: The Hacker News reports a new wave of refrigeration cyberattacks hitting supermarkets across Europe, forcing stores to pull food.

Help Net Security reports attackers are exploiting critical Node-RED flaw CVE-2026-58115 to deploy a Linux bot and backdoors. The Hacker News ties the same CVE to Siemens IoT2050 devices, where it is used to plant remote command backdoors.

Connect Secure, 4 outlets: Ivanti patched two more zero-days chained in attacks, CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527. CISA KEV lists CVE-2026-104935 in the same product, with federal due dates of 2026-11-02 and 2026-11-13.
Binance, 7 outlets: The Register reports the FBI pins the $6.3B heist on North Korean hackers. SecurityWeek says the FBI flagged over 600 addresses tied to it.

actions: Find Node-RED instances and Siemens IoT2050 devices, patch CVE-2026-58115 per vendor guidance, and look for backdoors. Isolate exposed ones you cannot patch.
Patch GitLab CE/EE (CVE-2026-97229) and Cisco ASA/FTD (CVE-2026-76418) now; both KEV due dates have passed. Check GitLab servers for signs of RCE.
Apply Ivanti's latest Connect Secure patches, covering CVE-2026-111357 and CVE-2026-118527, and check appliances for compromise.
Update DSM on Synology NAS devices, restrict their internet exposure, and confirm backups are intact.
If you run a CryptoPayment gateway, restrict access until CVE-2026-81648 is patched and rotate any wallet credentials it holds.
If you use Cursor, review installed extensions for the malicious Claude Code extension SecurityWeek reports was served in a supply chain attack.
